chapter: New York 1936-39 (second pass of the transcript)
title: Talbot band personnel and Black Cat sit-ins (second pass)
summary: Repeat of personnel and the Goodman and Lester Young battle on Honeysuckle Rose.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it

blocks.x: Yeah. Now, who was in the Skeets Talbot band?

Carl Teddy Smith had been with Basie. The rest of the guys you wouldn't know. Lem Johnson was a piano player, Freddy Jefferson was a piano player and Charles Bloomer was a drummer who, he and I joined Benny Goodman on a Camel Caravan show in '39. Skeets Talbot was the arranger, he's a professor in Texas. That was it. But every night John would bring a different group of people down and they would sit in.

They would sit in. Benny Goodman and Lester Young had a battle of music that we played Honeysuckle Rose for 45 minutes and in the interchange, Lester played his clarinet and Benny played his tenor and music hadn't been going for 45 minutes at that period of time.
That was fantastic. And Herschell Evans was there. Buck Clayton, Walter Page, Dave -- drummer with Woody Herman.
Dave Tuft. Joe Jones, all these kinds of people used to come down every night. You know. And they had a big furnace downstairs, this was, we'd go
downstairs and turn on. We'd go down there and learn to smoke pot. But it was fantastic, but from seven to four seven nights a week.
How long were the sets usually? I mean, well, you didn't have someone sitting in in that situation where it might just, you know, just like 45 minute sets and 15 off or --
Oh, no, this was a specialty then, this was like a show. This was the show thing. Well, we had a show, we had people performing you know, a regular routine but when these guests came --
